From 0f42e3f4fe2a58394e37241d02d9ca6ab7b7d516 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jiayuan Chen <jiayuan.chen@linux.dev>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 09:45:12 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] net: skb: fix cross-cache free of KFENCE-allocated skb head

SKB_SMALL_HEAD_CACHE_SIZE is intentionally set to a non-power-of-2
value (e.g. 704 on x86_64) to avoid collisions with generic kmalloc
bucket sizes. This ensures that skb_kfree_head() can reliably use
skb_end_offset to distinguish skb heads allocated from
skb_small_head_cache vs. generic kmalloc caches.

However, when KFENCE is enabled, kfence_ksize() returns the exact
requested allocation size instead of the slab bucket size. If a caller
(e.g. bpf_test_init) allocates skb head data via kzalloc() and the
requested size happens to equal SKB_SMALL_HEAD_CACHE_SIZE, then
slab_build_skb() -> ksize() returns that exact value. After subtracting
skb_shared_info overhead, skb_end_offset ends up matching
SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM, causing skb_kfree_head() to incorrectly free
the object to skb_small_head_cache instead of back to the original
kmalloc cache, resulting in a slab cross-cache free:

  kmem_cache_free(skbuff_small_head): Wrong slab cache. Expected
  skbuff_small_head but got kmalloc-1k

Fix this by always calling kfree(head) in skb_kfree_head(). This keeps
the free path generic and avoids allocator-specific misclassification
for KFENCE objects.

Fixes: bf9f1baa279f ("net: add dedicated kmem_cache for typical/small skb->head")
Reported-by: Antonius <antonius@bluedragonsec.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/CAK8a0jxC5L5N7hq-DT2_NhUyjBxrPocoiDazzsBk4TGgT1r4-A@mail.gmail.com/
Signed-off-by: Jiayuan Chen <jiayuan.chen@linux.dev>
Reviewed-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260403014517.142550-1-jiayuan.chen@linux.dev
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/core/skbuff.c b/net/core/skbuff.c
index 0e217041958a..43ee86dcf2ea 100644
--- a/net/core/skbuff.c
+++ b/net/core/skbuff.c
@@ -1083,10 +1083,7 @@ static int skb_pp_frag_ref(struct sk_buff *skb)
 
 static void skb_kfree_head(void *head, unsigned int end_offset)
 {
-	if (end_offset == SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM)
-		kmem_cache_free(net_hotdata.skb_small_head_cache, head);
-	else
-		kfree(head);
+	kfree(head);
 }
 
 static void skb_free_head(struct sk_buff *skb)
-- 
2.34.1

### Modifications in Each File

- **net/core/skbuff.c**: In the function `skb_kfree_head()`, the conditional logic that checked `end_offset == SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM` to decide between `kmem_cache_free()` for objects from the `skb_small_head_cache` and `kfree()` for other kmalloc-allocated heads was removed. Now, `kfree(head)` is called unconditionally.

### Relationship of Modifications

The bug occurred because KFENCE’s `kfence_ksize()` returns the exact requested allocation size, not the slab bucket size. When a caller (e.g., `bpf_test_init`) allocated an skb head of a size equal to `SKB_SMALL_HEAD_CACHE_SIZE`, `ksize()` returned that exact value, causing `skb_end_offset` to match `SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM`. The original conditional then incorrectly freed the KFENCE-allocated object to the `skb_small_head_cache` instead of its original kmalloc cache, leading to a slab cross-cache free.

By replacing the conditional with a direct `kfree()`, the free path becomes independent of the allocator’s size-reporting behavior. This avoids misclassification for KFENCE objects while remaining safe for all skb heads (since `kfree()` works correctly for both kmalloc allocations and, in this context, objects from `skb_small_head_cache` due to kernel internal consistency). The change eliminates the root cause without altering the allocation logic.

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by the conditional logic in `skb_kfree_head()` that uses `end_offset` (derived from `skb_end_offset`, which itself relies on `ksize()`) to decide whether to free an skb head to `skb_small_head_cache` via `kmem_cache_free()` or to general memory via `kfree()`. When KFENCE is enabled, `kfence_ksize()` returns the exact requested allocation size rather than the slab bucket size. If a caller allocates an skb head with a size exactly equal to `SKB_SMALL_HEAD_CACHE_SIZE`, `ksize()` returns that exact value, causing `skb_end_offset` to match `SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM`. This causes `skb_kfree_head()` to incorrectly free the object to `skb_small_head_cache` (which expects only objects allocated from that dedicated cache) instead of back to the original kmalloc cache, resulting in a slab cross-cache free.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void skb_kfree_head(void *head, unsigned int end_offset)
 {
-	if (end_offset == SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM)
-		kmem_cache_free(net_hotdata.skb_small_head_cache, head);
-	else
-		kfree(head);
+	kfree(head);
 }
